proposition: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, the sum of k^3 for k = 1..n equals (n(n+1)/2)^2.
hypotheses: the sum is empty for n = 0

argument.text: At n = 1, the sum of k^3 for k = 1..n = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, n^2 + 1 exceeds n.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 30 for which n^2 > 10.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, at least one of the following holds: n mod 3 = 0; n mod 3 = 1; n mod 3 = 2.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, n^2 is congruent to (n^2) + 357 modulo 119.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
The steps above establish the statement up to 30, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 30.
